summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for key-only SSH access using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node with ansible-core installed). The playbook (idempotent, /root/ansible-opsadmin/site.yml on node2) creates the opsadmin user, installs the specified ed25519 public key as its sole authorized key, and enforces PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no in sshd_config with a validated reload handler. Verified end-to-end: password auth for opsadmin is rejected (publickey-only offered), and a test-key login as opsadmin succeeded before authorized_keys was restored to exactly the required key. Also fixed a pre-existing issue on node1 blocking any SSH access: missing SSH host keys were causing ssh.service to crash-loop and its socket to hit the failure-start limit; regenerated host keys with ssh-keygen -A and reset/started ssh.socket. Completed the mandatory restart protocol for both nodes: captured pre-restart boot IDs and health, restarted node1 then node2 one at a time via shutdown -r now, confirmed each node's boot_id changed post-restart, and reverified opsadmin/sshd config persistence on node1 and the ansible/SSH control setup on node2 afterward.

Diagnosed and fixed node1's missing SSH host keys (ssh.service was crash-looping / ssh.socket hit service-start-limit-hit); ran ssh-keygen -A and reset/started ssh.socket

Playbook creates opsadmin user, installs exclusive authorized_key with the specified ed25519 key, and sets PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no with a validated sshd reload handler
